marta: quick heads-up — did a bring-up comparison between rankformer-v2 (fp16) and mini-rerank-3b-ptq on three eval sets (MSMARCO dev, ELI5 QA subset, internal-support-queries). seeing a consistent NDCG@10 regression on very short queries when doc shape is "bullet-list" vs "paragraph". attaching quick notes and commands below.

samir: numbers? how big is the regression and which bucket?

marta: small but consistent: on short queries (<6 tokens) rankformer-v2 fp16 NDCG@10=0.318, mini-ptq int8 NDCG@10=0.260 on internal-support-queries w/ bullet-list docs. that's ~0.058 absolute. paragraph docs are closer (0.316 vs 0.304).

ryan: interesting. any tokenizer mismatch between the two pipelines? ptq harness used the model tokenizer or the eval-harness tokenizer?

marta: used model tokenizer for both, but the inputizer step for bullet-list inserts list markers and \"- \" which shifts tokenization. suspected that candidate normalization + prefix tokens amplify quant noise on short queries.

hana: we should bucket by query intent too (clarification vs factual). short clarifying queries might be more sensitive. also run a paired bootstrap for significance.

marta: agreed. sample sizes: short queries bucket=1,120 queries; paragraph-format short bucket=1,050. paired bootstrap p~0.03 for internal-support-queries.

samir: can you paste the eval command you ran? makes repro faster.

marta: here you go:
```
python eval_harness.py --model mini-rerank-3b-ptq --quant-config int8-gemm --dataset internal-support --doc-format bullet-list --metric ndcg@10 --buckets "q_len:<=6" --seed 42 --save-run /tmp/run_ptq_bullet.json
```

ryan: two quick asks: 1) try normalizing candidate text (strip list markers, collapse whitespace) before tokenization; 2) simulate cache-warm vs cache-cold for sequential rerank calls, PTQ might be worse when KV cache is fragmented.

marta: will add normalization step and rerun with warm/cold simulation.

eval-bot: quick summary from /tmp/run_ptq_bullet.json ->
NDCG@10 (short, bullet-list):
- rankformer-v2 fp16: 0.318
- mini-rerank-3b-ptq int8-gemm: 0.260
MRR@10 (short, bullet-list): 0.410 vs 0.362
(bootstrap 1k samples, p=0.028)

hana: thanks. also add a slice for presence_of_code_blocks and for doc-length<120 tokens. those are orthogonal.

samir: what quant config did you use? int8-gemm or asymmetric? might try out per-channel quant for attention weights.

marta: int8-gemm with symmetric clipping, outlier removal threshold=3.0. I'll try per-channel and int4-gemm-slow tomorrow.

ryan: small nit — make sure the eval harness uses identical padding/truncation rules for both models. mismatch there can cause faux regressions.

marta: yep, used config file shared in repo: \"eval/configs/re-rank-standard.yaml\" — includes pad_to_max=False, truncate_right=True, max_doc_tokens=512.

marta: running overnight: normalization + per-channel int8 + cache-warm sim. will post results in this thread. opening a tiny PR to expose the bucket definitions and seed in the harness so results are reproducible. :eyes:

hana: appreciated. if the regression persists after per-channel, we should run a small manual inspection of top 20 queries where predictions flip. may reveal ordering artifacts due to punctuation and list markers.

samir: also try eval on MS MARCO with synthetic bullet-list (convert paras->list) to see if effect is dataset-specific or formatting-specific.

marta: good call — I'll synthetic-convert MS MARCO and include that run.

eval-bot: note: run queued on remote GPU cluster (job 9923). ETA ~3h. will publish metrics + top-20 flip diffs to /artifacts/9923ummary.json when done.

ryan: thanks — fyi if anyone else wants to reproduce quickly: seed 42, tokenizer v1.3.0, eval-harness commit sha: 8a2f9b3.

marta: perfect. thanks all. will post final numbers and candidate diffs once job finishes. :thumbsup:
